title: 340 MB of Playwright screenshot baselines are committed to git, 29 of them byte-identical copies, and are most of the 628 MB .git.

source.ref: Whole-site audit 2026-11-16 (project thread, requested by Daniel). Confidence: CONFIRMED. Audit file: audit/FINAL-BUILD-AND-REPAIR-LIST-2026-11-16.md

detail:
EVIDENCE: test/e2e/__screenshots__/visual.spec.ts/ holds 154 tracked PNGs, ~347 MB (git ls-files | du). 29 files share an md5 with another (e.g. about--dawn-light-desktop.png == about--midnight-light-desktop.png, both 798d6638...). .gitattributes has no LFS rule; .git is 628M.

WHY IT MATTERS: Every clone, CI checkout and cloud agent session pulls ~0.6 GB. Slower clones and CI; baselines churn adds to history forever.

FIX DIRECTION: Move baselines to Git LFS or an artifact store, and de-duplicate identical dawn/midnight captures (or skip the redundant variant).

2026-11-16 (dedupe, row stays open): the 29 byte-identical midnight-light PNGs are deleted; each is listed in test/e2e/__screenshots__/shared-baselines.json and its test reads the dawn-light file (test/e2e/shared-baselines.ts, scripts/dedupe-visual-baselines.mjs in the capture job). Tracked baselines: 154 PNGs / 355.7 MB -> 125 PNGs / 256.4 MB. Identical files already shared one git blob, so .git and clone transfer do not shrink; the saving is 99.3 MB of checkout. Git LFS was NOT added (owner rule 2026-11-16: only if clearly inside the free tier). GitHub Free includes 10 GiB LFS bandwidth per month and Actions downloads count against it. The PNG bytes are read by ci.yml's vitest job (baseline-distinctness, screenshot-tolerance) and by e2e.yml's visual compare: 4,899 and 2,958 runs in the 30 days to 2026-11-15. At 0.239 GiB per pull that is about 1,170 GiB and 706 GiB a month, against 10. The probe (tracked baselines at or under 50 MB) still fails. Remaining routes: an artifact store outside git, or a smaller capture set.

verify.note: Fails on 2026-11-16 (audit run). Passes when the fix lands. Audit-written probes are direction checks; retime only with Daniel's phrase.
